newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks to rebound after yesterday's dip.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks to rebound after yesterday's dip.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to attempt a rebound on Thursday after the market benchmark briefly pierced below the 20,000 barrier on Wednesday, brokers said.
They said U.S. markets were firm overnight and this was likely to provide support, but eyes would be on financial sector shares and Sony Corp for signs of recovery.

On Wednesday, the 225-share Nikkei average gained 20.90 points or 0.10 percent to close at 20,196.42, after breaking the 20,000 barrier for the first time since May 28. Its September futures ended 120 points higher at 20,220.
"There was no heavy selling, however, and stocks drifted in thin trade," he added.
Turnover was a dismal 127 million shares, down from the trade of 141 million shares at the end of the morning session on Wednesday. Losers beat winners 624 to 350, while 223 issues were unchanged.

Brokers said that although the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting ended on Wednesday without a rate hike, some investors were still waiting for U.S. payroll data due out later on Thursday, heightening the cautious mood.

Sony Corp's shares had slipped 150 yen to 9,620 by midday. This was partly due to profit-taking and to news that Morgan Stanley strategist Alexander Kinmont had recently reduced the electrical sector 0#ELC.T weighting to 23 percent from 32 percent.

"As far as high-techs are concerned, there are worries about a slowdown in the U.S. markets, a cool summer in Japan and speculation that the sector's earnings growth may have peaked in the first half of the business year," a trader at a foreign brokerage said. "Sony led the sector higher so it's only natural that investors are tempted to sell."
Brokers said that most investors continued to dabble in individual issues, and no distinct trading trend was detected.
Stocks that could be affected by the oil spill on Wednesday attracted attention. A supertanker scraped a reef and sprang a leak on Wednesday.

Shares of Nippon Yusen KK, whose subsidiary operates the tanker, fell eight yen to 424. Nomura Securities also cut its rating for the firm. The "Big Four" brokerage said the direct impact from the accident was likely to be light but the accident would probably hurt the firm's image and its costs may increase in the aftermath of the accident.
Shares of Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd, which chartered the tanker, were down 13 yen at 499.

Hopes that demand for oil fences would rise lifted shares of Bridgestone Corp, which is the world's largest tyre maker and a leading domestic producer of oil fences. Its shares had added 70 yen to reach 2,660 by midday.
By sector, trading houses, oil, transport equipment, mining and real estate were at the top of the list of decliners.
Credit/lease, rubber, fisheries, miscellaneous manufacturers and pharmaceuticals headed the list of gainers.
The TOPIX index fell 0.63 point or 0.04 percent to 1,530.64. The Nikkei 300 rose 0.07 point or 0.02 percent to end the two-hour session at 296.94.
